Warehouses & logistics.

We plan roof, drainage, lighting and building repairs around stock, loading movements and the routes your warehouse needs to use.

Stage the work around live loading.

A warehouse maintenance scope needs to identify the space below the repair as well as the defect itself. We confirm loading activity, storage areas, pedestrian routes and equipment access, then agree how each work zone is released and returned.

01 / Warehouse exterior and traffic approach

Roofline to loading area

A leaking roof above stock, a damaged dock door and a failed pavement patch have different impacts. Mark delivery slots and forklift routes together with the affected zone. If a bay closes, agree a replacement route, storage protection and the conditions for vehicles to return.

We map roof drip positions against rack bays, dock doors and vehicle routes, and note whether water appears during rain or later. The warehouse contact confirms stock relocation or covers, and which dock and lanes can remain active. Roof access above and any protected area below are scheduled as one work package.

  • Roof and rainwater

    We record reported leaks, roof details, box gutters, outlets and downstream drainage. The affected stock or working area is included when planning access and protection.

  • Building fabric and lighting

    Agreed door, cladding, high-level lighting and building defects are identified by location, height and the equipment or space required to reach them.

  • External surfaces and access

    We scope local paving, concrete, drainage and fixed access-item defects with delivery, loading and pedestrian movements in view.

02 / Marked vehicle and pedestrian circulation surface

Release the area, then run the work

  1. 01

    Confirm the operating plan

    We agree the affected zone and the nominated site contact. Vehicle, forklift and pedestrian activity is discussed alongside the proposed work.

  2. 02

    Coordinate access and materials

    We identify equipment space, deliveries, storage protection and any service interruption. Connected repairs are ordered before final finishes.

  3. 03

    Check and return the zone

    We record the completed scope and the conditions for reopening. Any further investigation, parts or follow-up remain separate from completed work.

One defect or a planned zone of work

A damaged threshold at an active bay affects loading as well as the building. Record the vehicle route, available alternate bay and the check the warehouse team needs before reopening the lane.

Price single fittings after checking condition and access. Review recurring roof, drain or surface defects together and plan by zone.

Materials, installation height, the condition below the surface, equipment access and operating restrictions influence the work package. We identify investigation separately where the cause is concealed.

Send the defect with its operating context

  • Location and history

    Include a site or bay reference, the fault pattern, photographs and any previous repair records.

  • Movements and availability

    Identify loading periods, routes, stock that needs protection and available inspection or attendance windows.

Release bays one stage at a time.

We identify usable bays, remaining restrictions and observations after rain or traffic where agreed.

Keep the property record useful

We tie completion photographs and notes to the defined zone and repaired item. Where the problem depends on rainfall or operating conditions, any agreed follow-up observation is recorded with the original history.

We record which bays are active, which doors form part of vehicle routes and where stock can be moved. A surface repair near a dock requires an agreed protection plan and a release point that warehouse staff can verify before resuming movements.

  • Dock and traffic plan
  • Stock protection and bay staging
  • Restrictions and release

Common questions

Can roof work happen while stock remains below?
Check the work area and the space below. Include stock protection and zone release conditions in the brief.
Can we repair only part of a loading area?
We define the defect, substrate and route arrangements before agreeing a local repair. Material curing and the intended traffic use determine the conditions for returning that section to service.
Can a loading bay stay open during repairs?
Confirm the separation from work, vehicle clearances and traffic arrangements first. Some work requires temporary closure and an alternative bay.
